restoration_note: Teaching describes the two sorrows of sun and moon — Divine Truth in its illuminating and reflective manifestations — who, though stationed firm and casting no shadow, grieve over (1) the King of Darkness/proprium enthroned as counterfeit king-face, and (2) the Living Soul dispersed and transmigrated body to body. Most gaps are line-break completions (ⲣⲱⲙⲉ, ϩⲟⲗⲟⲧⲉⲗⲱⲥ, ⲥⲉⲙⲟⲩϩ, ⲡⲥⲁⲛⲧⲡⲉ, ⲁⲣⲁⲥ, ⲛϩⲏⲧ, ⲧⲙⲁϩⲥⲛⲉⲩ, ⲛⲑⲗⲓⲯⲓⲥ, ⲡⲓⲛⲉⲩ, ⲡϣⲁⲣⲡ, ⲡϩⲁⲏ) tightly constrained by visible traces. Key spiritual restorations: {10} ⲥⲱⲧⲙⲉ as 'Hearing' (paired with ⲧⲱⲍⲙⲉ Call); {29} the eschatological binding into the bolos. The three-gap stretch {6}-{8}, plus {20} (a 2-char interior lacuna) and {22} (4-char lacuna), have too few traces to constrain confidently and are left unrestorable.

restorations.basis: Editor fill confirmed: ⲩ[ⲁ]ⲟⲩⲉ = ⲗⲁⲟⲩⲉ 'any one' with ⲙⲛ̄ negation = 'no one of men.'
Editor fill: relative-locative 'who is in the world standing on his feet.' Tentative but syntactically required to link 'no one of men' with 'standing in the world.'
ⲍⲛ̄ (Lyc. for ϩⲛ̄), with ⲛ̄ visible. Standard preposition before ⲟⲩ-noun.
ⲟⲩ[ⲧ]ⲱⲧ 'an agreement/accord'; visible ⲟⲩ...ⲱⲧ frame requires single internal letter; 'in an agreement of...' fits the cosmic-station thought.
[ⲡⲣⲉ]ⲱⲉ = ⲡⲣⲁⲱⲉ/ⲡⲣⲉϣⲉ 'joy' (Lyc.); 'joy lasting forth until the end' fits the chapter's framing of permanent state, and ⲣⲁⲱⲉ recurs throughout.
Completes ⲣⲱⲙⲉ 'men' across the line break (ⲣⲱ visible at end of preceding line); ⲟⲩ ⲙⲟⲛⲟⲛ ⲛ̄ⲣⲱⲙⲉ ... ⲁⲗⲗⲁ 'not only men ... but also (sun/moon).'

3-char lacuna with no surrounding traces. Cannot determine whether this begins a new clause or continues the sun-and-moon description; multiple possible fills (ⲛⲉⲓ, ⲛⲉⲧ, ⲛⲁⲩ, etc.) cannot be discriminated.

5-char lacuna with partial 'ⲉ . . ⲏⲧⲉ.' Possibilities like ⲉⲣⲏⲧⲉ (foot), ⲉⲩⲣⲏⲧⲉ (their foot), or other ⲉ-?-?-ⲏⲧⲉ forms cannot be securely distinguished from the spiritual context alone; honest non-restoration is preferable.
2-char lacuna with no traces, dependent on the unrestorable {7}. Insufficient constraint.
[ⲁ]ⲍⲉ ⲁⲣⲉⲧⲟⲩ = ⲁϩⲉ ⲉⲣⲁⲧⲟⲩ 'they stand on their feet'; standard idiom of fixed station echoing line 4 ⲉϩⲁⲍⲉ ⲁⲣⲉⲧϥ̄.
Completes ⲥⲱⲧⲙⲉ. Reading as the noun 'Hearing' (lexicon: ⲡⲥⲱⲧⲙⲉ, response to the Call) — pairs with preceding ⲟⲩⲧⲱⲍⲙⲉ 'a summons-forth': 'in a Call and a Hearing' — the luminaries' apostolic station.
Completes ϩⲟⲗⲟⲧⲉⲗⲱⲥ 'wholly' (Greek ὁλοτελῶς) across line break; ⲉ̄ visible (= ⲥ).
Completes ⲥⲉⲙⲟⲩϩ 'they are filled'; ϩ visible. Idiom ⲙⲟⲩϩ ⲛ̄ⲥⲱ⸗ 'be filled with concern after.'
Completes ⲥⲉⲛⲉⲩ 'they see'; ⲉⲩ visible. The luminaries see the king-face of the upper-place.
Completes ⲡⲥⲁⲛⲧⲡⲉ 'the upper place'; paired with ⲡⲥⲁⲛⲙ̄ⲓ̈ⲧⲛⲉ 'lower place' immediately following.
Completes ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'forth' (ⲃⲁⲗ visible at line 14 start); ⲟⲩⲃⲱⲗⲧ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'a release-forth' (cf. lexicon ⲃⲱⲗ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ).
Completes ⲛϩⲏⲧ in idiom ⲡⲉϩⲱⲕ ⲛϩⲏⲧ 'his heart's desire'; ⲛϩⲏ visible.
Completes ⲧⲙⲁϩⲥⲛⲉⲩ 'the second (reason)'; ⲁϩⲥⲛⲉⲩ visible. Marks the second cause of incomplete joy, paired with ⲟⲩⲉ ⲙⲉⲛ above.
Begins ⲁⲣⲁⲥ 'to her'; ⲣⲁⲥ visible at start of next line.
Completes ⲁⲣⲁⲥ 'to her' from preceding line; ⲥ visible.

2-char interior lacuna in ⲥⲁ??ϩ. No standard Coptic word with this exact frame (ⲥⲁ-X-X-ϩ) is constrained by context; though the spiritual reading suggests dispersal/stretching, candidates (ⲥⲁⲣⲡϣ̄, ⲥⲁⲡⲱϩ, etc.) are speculative. Honest non-restoration.
Completes ⲛ̄ⲧⲡⲉ 'of the upper place'; ⲡⲉ visible, paired with ⲡⲥⲁⲛⲙ̄ⲓ̈ⲧⲛⲉ following.
4-char lacuna with no traces, between 'tree and thorn' and 'in every affliction.' Could be a connector (ⲁⲩⲱ), a circumstantial subject (ⲉⲩⲍⲛ̄), or another paired term. Insufficient constraint.
Completes ⲙ̄ⲙⲁⲥ from preceding ⲙⲁ + circumstantial ⲉⲩ-prefix on the next verb; standard editorial restoration.
Circumstantial subject prefix ⲉⲩ- on ϣⲱⲗ 'plunder'; required by parallel ⲉⲩⲡⲧⲱⲛⲉ following.
Completes ⲙⲉⲣⲓⲧ 'beloved' (qualitative); ⲙⲉⲣⲓ visible. The Living Soul as ⲙⲉⲣⲓⲧ before the luminaries.
Completes ⲛⲑⲗⲓⲯⲓⲥ (Greek θλίψις) across line break; ⲛⲑ on this line, ⲯⲓⲥ visible at start of next.
Completes ⲉⲩⲣⲉϣⲉ 'they rejoicing' (circumstantial); ⲉ at start and ⲣⲉϣⲉ at end visible.
Preposition ϩⲙ̄ before ⲡⲉⲧⲉ ⲡⲧⲱϩ ⲉⲛ ⲡⲉ 'that to which it does not befit' — the false enthronement of the enemy.

After ⲥⲁⲩϩϥ̄ ⲁϩⲟⲩⲛ 'gather him inward,' the eschatological terminus is the bolos — the final compacted state of evil sealed at the consummation (lexicon ⲡⲃⲱⲗⲟⲥ). Standard Manichaean motif of binding the enemy in the bolos before ϣⲁ ⲁⲛⲏϩⲉ 'for ever.'
Completes ⲁⲧϩⲁⲏ 'at the end' (Lyc. for ⲉⲡϩⲁⲏ); ⲁⲧ visible at end of preceding line, ⲏ at start of next. The eschatological terminus, paralleling ⲧⲍⲁⲏ above.
Completes ⲙ̄ⲡⲓⲛⲉⲩ 'this moment'; ⲙ̄ⲡⲓⲛ visible. Marks the eschatological turning-point after which grief ceases.
ⲭⲛ̄ ⲛ̄ϣⲁⲣⲡ̄ 'from the beginning/first' (lexicon: ⲡϣⲁⲣⲡ̄ = first/primal); the original primal state of the luminaries, continuous ϣⲁ ⲁⲛⲏϩⲉ 'forever' on the next line. Cosmological terminus a quo.
